description: A Leaflet choropleth of US states with clearly labeled placeholder values. Learners move four ordered color thresholds or pick presets, watch the map and class counts update, and judge whether each setting reveals or hides a south-north gradient and a Great Lakes cluster.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Choropleth class thresholds and the patterns they reveal or hide
learningObjectives: The learner will judge whether a set of color thresholds reveals or hides a geographic pattern in a dataset.
prerequisites: Choropleth maps and the template threshold function (Chapter 9)
Reading a legend with value ranges

dependencies: us-states.json GeoJSON from the map template's public URL (raw.githubusercontent.com, fetched at load)

accessibility.notes: Sliders, select, checkbox and buttons are native controls with labels; the info panel names the class number and range, and the legend lists ranges and counts, so color is not the only channel; legend and feedback are aria-live

dataFiles: data.json (placeholder value per state, color scale, presets, cluster list)

controls.label: Threshold 1-4
controls.purpose: Class breaks between the five colors, kept in increasing order

controls.label: Preset
controls.purpose: Load a named set of thresholds

controls.label: Show values on hover
controls.purpose: Show or hide the numeric value in the info panel

controls.label: Reset view
controls.purpose: Return to the initial map extent

controls.label: North-south gradient / Great Lakes trend
controls.purpose: The learner's judgment for each pattern

controls.label: Check
controls.purpose: Compare the judgment with the class counts

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Judge-then-check with presets that each reveal one pattern and hide another
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Parameter sliders on a choropleth with an evaluation prompt and feedback
keyQuestions: Which preset shows the south-north gradient, and which hides it?
Why do the template thresholds split the Great Lakes cluster?
Can one set of five classes reveal both patterns, and at what cost?
commonMisconceptions: The map shows the data as it is (the thresholds decide what is visible)
Equal intervals are always neutral (they can hide variation inside a dense range)
Two regions with the same color have similar values (61 and 80 can share a class)
assessmentOpportunities: Accuracy of the revealed/hidden judgments across presets
Justification of a custom threshold set

simulation.modelType: Threshold classification of a continuous value into five classes
equations: class = 5 if v > t4; 4 if v > t3; 3 if v > t2; 2 if v > t1; else 1
equal intervals: t_k = min + k * (max - min) / 5
a pattern counts as revealed when its regions span at least 3 classes
assumptions: Values are invented placeholders built to contain two patterns
limitations: The revealed/hidden rule is a simple class-count heuristic, not a statistical test
